Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a Chemical Cross-Linking Mass Spectrometry (CXMS) study using the BS3 crosslinker. While not a traditional TPP (Thermal Proteome Profiling) assay, CXMS is often routed through similar structural proteomics modifiers (mod_tpp) or specific CXMS pipelines. Acquisition is DDA based on the description of precursor and fragment ion scans. Search parameters explicitly include phosphorylation and BS3-linked Lysine.

organism: KRAS (human, residues 1-169) bound to intact BRAF (human) in an autoinhibited state with MEK1 (human, ) and a 14-3-3 (SF9) dimer
cell_lines: isolation of the fully processed KRAS4b protein from infected Sf9 insect cells (Gibbo Sf9 cells, cat.no. 11496015)
co-expressed with MEK1WT or MEK1SASA, respectively, in baculovirus/insect cell expression system with Sf9 cells
scope: The complex of BRAF, MEK1, and insect cell derived 14-3-3 ε, ζ co-purified through Ni-NTA- and Strep- affinity chromatography and finally through size-exclusion chromatography
analyzed via LC-MS/MS KRAS (human, residues 1-169) bound to intact BRAF (human) in an autoinhibited state with MEK1 (human, ) and a 14-3-3 (SF9) dimer
Complexes cross-linked with BS3 were denatured in 8 M urea and subjected to reduction and carbamidomethylation with TCEP and iodoacetamide. Samples were diluted to 2 M urea and digested with trypsin

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The analyzed material was a reconstituted protein complex consisting of human KRAS, BRAF, and MEK1, and Sf9-derived 14-3-3, purified via affinity chromatography and size-exclusion chromatography before being cross-linked and analyzed by MS.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics (CXMS) experiment specifically analyzes the assembly and inter-domain interactions of the KRAS/BRAF/MEK1/14-3-3 complex compared to the RAS-free state. BS3 is used as a cross-linking reagent for structural probing, not as a biological perturbation.
